facts.claim: The travel blog Hello Jetlag's Kakaako guide (March 12, 2019) describes Cafe Duck Butt as a local Korean bar for karaoke, K-pop videos, Korean food and 'soju out of a watermelon,' with 'a bit of a hole in the wall, dive bar vibe,' housed in a nondescript warehouse that can be hard to find.
facts.source_title: A Guide to Kakaako // Mural Hunting in Honolulu's Coolest Neighborhood - Hello Jetlag
facts.verbatim_snippet: Cafe Duck Butt is a local Korean bar where you can sing karaoke, watch K-pop music videos, eat Korean food and drink soju out of a watermelon. It has a bit of a hole in the wall, dive bar vibe but you can't beat the $1/song karaoke.
facts.notes: Same page: 'The bar is located in a nondescript warehouse and can be a little hard to find'; happy hour 5pm–8pm; recommends the kimchee pancakes and soju. The $1/song figure is recorded separately as conflicting.

facts.claim: Media and guides consistently characterize Café Duck Butt as a dive bar / hole-in-the-wall in a windowless Kakaako building: Honolulu Magazine files it under dive bars (2022), the Star-Advertiser calls it a 'windowless bar and karaoke joint' (2015) and a 'windowless lounge' (2018), and Hello Jetlag cites its 'dive bar vibe' (2019).
facts.source_title: Pau Hana Patrol column - Honolulu Star-Advertiser
facts.verbatim_snippet: Cafe Duck Butt is a windowless lounge in Kakaako that opened eight years ago
facts.notes: Same 2018 column adds that it 'drew crowds craving its spicy, tantalizing Korean tacos, crunchy fried chicken and pitchers of flavored soju cocktails.' Only this Café Duck Butt sentence is recorded; the column's main subject (the excluded Kapolei spinoff) is ignored. Corroborating sources: honolulumagazine.com 6 'Ono Dive Bars (2022), staradvertiser.com Top restaurants A-Z (2015), hellojetlag.com (2019).

facts.claim: K-pop is a recurring descriptor: sources describe the main room playing K-pop music videos (Honolulu Magazine), 'watch K-pop music videos' (Hello Jetlag), and a TripAdvisor review titled 'K-Pop, Karaoke and Korean Food....What Could Go Wrong??'
facts.source_title: K-Pop, Karaoke and Korean Food....What Could Go Wrong?? - Review of Cafe Duck Butt - Tripadvisor
facts.verbatim_snippet: K-Pop, Karaoke and Korean Food....What Could Go Wrong??
facts.notes: TripAdvisor item is a user review title (user-generated). Corroborated by honolulumagazine.com/drinks-and-pupu-in-hawaii/ ('the main room plays K-pop music videos on eight large TV screens') and hellojetlag.com ('watch K-pop music videos').

facts.claim: The per-song karaoke price is reported inconsistently: $1/song (Hello Jetlag 2019; a Yelp reviewer) versus $2/song (Hawaii Travel Spot 2023; Wanderlog reviewers, who also cite a $150 food-and-drink minimum to reserve a room).
facts.source_title: Where to Find the Best Karaoke in Honolulu (2023) - Hawaii Travel Spot
facts.verbatim_snippet: Here you will find private rooms for karaoke, and it costs $2 per song.
facts.notes: hellojetlag.com (2019-03-12): 'you can't beat the $1/song karaoke'; a Yelp reviewer: 'The karaoke is only $1 per song (most other places charge $2)'; Wanderlog review summary: 'you need to spend $150 on food and drinks to be able to reserve the karaoke rooms at $2.00 a song.' All prices unconfirmed by the owner and may reflect changes over time.

facts.claim: Hawaii Travel Spot's 2023 best-karaoke list includes Cafe Duck Butt, noting private karaoke rooms, 5 pm–2 am hours, and that it is 'famous for its watermelon drink'—half a watermelon filled with soju.

facts.verbatim_snippet: This cafe has mouth-watering food and drinks and is famous for its watermelon drink. You get half a watermelon filled with a soju drink you will love!
facts.notes: The watermelon soju as a signature is echoed by HAWAI'I Magazine ('their watermelon soju is hard to resist') and Hello Jetlag ('drink soju out of a watermelon'); Honolulu Magazine mentions a different Kakaako venue, Chingu, for an 'over-the-top watermelon soju'—not Duck Butt.

facts.claim: Yelp reviewers praise the flavored sojus as the best part of the bar, naming watermelon, taro, li hing and cereal milk sojus and a Melona soju; one reviewer panned the Lava Flow soju as too sweet with no alcohol.
